To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

molluscan neurons and other cells express a variety of voltage sensitive calcium channels, which are differentially expressed in different cells and which play a key role in the generation of firing properties, transmitter release, neurite outgrowth and growth cone behavior.
molluscan calcium currents can be classified into transient and sustained low voltage activated channels and into transient and sustained high voltage activated channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(1) the characterization of calcium channels in mollusc neurons and muscle cells, (2) the modulation of calcium channels by second messengers, and (3) the functional roles of the channels in the control of action potential properties, transmitter release, growth cone behavior and synapse formation.
the classification, the modulation, the calcium dependent inactivation and the functional roles of molluscan voltage gated calcium channels.
the characterization of voltage gated calcium channels in identified neurons of molluscan species, and their roles in the generation of firing pattern and in the release of transmittors and hormones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the calcium channels of molluscs are very useful to study the functional role of calcium channels, and that the calcium channel research in molluscs is very useful to understand the functional role of these channels.
calcium channels are important regulators of the electrical activity, the release of transmittors and hormones, and growth cone and neurite behavior.

the calcium channels of molluscs are similar to those of other animals, but that molluscs provide unique opportunities to further increase our knowledge of calcium channels and their functional roles in neuronal and muscle cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
molluscan preparations are very suitable for the study of calcium channels.
molluscs are a very valuable model for studying calcium channel function.
molluscan calcium currents are very useful tools to investigate the molecular and cellular mechanisms of calcium channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calcium channels are important in the regulation of the activity of neurons, muscle cells, endocrine cells, and growth cones.
molluscan calcium channel currents are very diverse and that they are modulated by a large number of transmitters and modulators.
calcium channel diversity is much larger than anticipated and that calcium channels in molluscans are not just a model for mammalian calcium channels but have their own unique properties.
